#### Author
Santiago Hernandez
#### Prompt
<html>
  <head>

  </head>
  <body>
    <p style="margin-top: 0px">
      I didn't specify the json body of the 2 numbers to be summed, explain 
      how it's working
    </p>
  </body>
</html>


#### Answer **
<html>
  <head>

  </head>
  <body>
    <p style="margin-top: 0px">
      The request shape was my choice &#8212; nothing in the prompt defined it, so I 
      picked a minimal one in <a href="#">server.go</a>:
    </p>
    <pre data-copilot-type="code-block" data-copilot-offset="179,259" data-copilot-content-offset="185,256" data-copilot-code-block-index="0" data-copilot-code-language="go"><code>type sumRequest struct {
	A float64 `json:&quot;a&quot;`
	B float64 `json:&quot;b&quot;`
}</code></pre>
    <p>
      So the endpoint expects:
    </p>
    <pre data-copilot-type="code-block" data-copilot-offset="287,330" data-copilot-content-offset="291,327" data-copilot-code-block-index="1"><code>POST /api/v1/sum
{&quot;a&quot;: 2, &quot;b&quot;: 3.5}</code></pre>
    <p>
      and replies with <code>sumResponse</code>:
    </p>
    <pre data-copilot-type="code-block" data-copilot-offset="365,392" data-copilot-content-offset="373,389" data-copilot-code-block-index="2" data-copilot-code-language="json"><code>{&quot;result&quot;: 5.5}</code></pre>
    <p>
      How it actually behaves:
    </p>
    <ul>
      <li>
        <code>json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&amp;req)</code> maps the <code>a</code>/<code>b</code> 
        struct tags to the fields. Matching is case-insensitive, so <code>{&quot;A&quot;:2,&quot;B&quot;:3}</code> 
        also works.
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Unknown fields are ignored</strong> &#8212; <code>{&quot;x&quot;:1,&quot;y&quot;:2}</code> 
        decodes fine but leaves both fields at their zero value, returning <code>{&quot;result&quot;:0}</code>. 
        Same for a missing field: <code>{&quot;a&quot;:5}</code> &#8594; <code>{&quot;result&quot;:5}</code>.
      </li>
      <li>
        Wrong types (<code>{&quot;a&quot;:&quot;2&quot;}</code>) or malformed 
        JSON cause <code>Decode</code> to error, and the handler returns 400 
        with <code>{&quot;error&quot;:&quot;invalid json body&quot;}</code>.
      </li>
      <li>
        <code>float64</code> means integers and decimals both work; very large 
        integers lose precision beyond 2^53.
      </li>
      <li>
        Any verb other than POST on that path is rejected by the mux with 405 
        (the <code>&quot;POST &quot;</code> pattern prefix in <code>newRouter</code>).
      </li>
    </ul>
    <p>
      If you want stricter behavior, the two common tweaks are:
    </p>
    <pre data-copilot-type="code-block" data-copilot-offset="1169,1255" data-copilot-content-offset="1175,1252" data-copilot-code-block-index="3" data-copilot-code-language="go"><code>dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
dec.DisallowUnknownFields() // reject {&quot;x&quot;:1}</code></pre>
    <p>
      and using <code>*float64</code> fields so you can tell &quot;missing&quot; from 
      &quot;zero&quot; and reject incomplete bodies. Let me know if you'd prefer 
      different field names (e.g. <code>num1</code>/<code>num2</code>) or an 
      array like <code>{&quot;numbers&quot;:[1,2]}</code> and I can show that 
      version.
    </p>
  </body>
</html>
